evidence: CURRENT-DESIGN.md:14-16 specifies one serialized writer, a separate reconciler, and latest committed intent; :30 makes /seat read applicable state/templates/overrides/rules itself. DESIGN-NOTES.md:149-150,164-165,238-239 confirms separate files, a shared checkout, independent reconciliation, and direct agent reads. Full-text search across all four reviewed docs for snapshot, consistent/coherent read, isolation, lock, retry, commit/revision view and equivalents found no reader boundary; DESIGN-NOTES.md:179's external-action current-intent check states an outcome but no coherent read mechanism. Git's glossary says the working tree contains HEAD 'plus any local changes that you have made but not yet committed' (https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary.html); thus a reader of the shared checkout can see one changed file before its related files and commit. A template/override/relationship mutation can be read mid-write, causing /seat to orient from mismatched state or reconciliation to act on intent that is not yet committed, contrary to latest-committed-intent and recoverable-operation requirements (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:92-98). This is an acknowledged design-stage detail, not evidence of actual data loss; specify how readers obtain one committed revision or retry across a write.
